variants: TRON 1 Std. Ed. and TRON 1 EDU Ed. on the specification page, each with point-foot, sole and wheeled foot ends. Arm, sensor and voice-interaction expansion kits are sold separately. LimX sells TRON 2, Oli and Luna as separate products, which this record does not cover.
availability_note: LimX's TRON 1 pages carry Buy Now buttons that open a Contact Sales form, which says "we will contact you within 24 hours to provide more detailed product information and solutions". The pages state no price and no order path.

hardware.compute: A 12th Gen Intel i3 CPU with 16 GB of memory and 512 GB of storage.
hardware.sensors: The specification table's sensor row lists an RGBD camera and an IMU that provides IMU data, and the page text does not preserve which edition carries the camera. The overview page describes a Sensor Expansion Kit that integrates LiDAR and a depth camera and a Voice Interaction Kit with an NVIDIA NX module and a microphone array.
hardware.actuation: Actuators with a rated torque of 30 N·m, a peak torque of 60 N·m and a peak speed of 15 rad/s, in a body of at most 392 x 420 x 845 mm and at most 20 kg, with a load capacity of up to 10 kg. Point-foot and sole speeds are listed below 1 m/s and wheeled speed at up to 3 m/s.
hardware.power: A 46.8 V, 4.5 Ah ternary lithium battery with a maximum power of 1,000 W, a range of up to 2 hours, quick battery swapping, and a charging time of under 1 hour from 20% to 80%.

developer_access: LimX's TRON 1 overview page lists a "Fully Open SDK and Hardware Interface", development "in Python, C++ not required", and a "Detailed user manual, professional secondary development guide and code examples". Its tron1-rl-deploy-ros repository says it will "Deploy trained reinforcement learning (RL) walking policies to TRON1 biped and wheel-legged robots via ROS Noetic" and "Loads ONNX models through `ros_control` and runs them on Gazebo simulation or real hardware". Its tron1-rl-isaaclab repository documents training PPO locomotion policies and extends Isaac Lab "to support sim-to-real training for TRON1 robot variants", and its tron1-agent repository documents a voice agent that relies on LLMs for dialogue and says it "supports Tron action execution calls".
terms_note: LimX's Terms & Policies page opens with an after-sales service policy for robotic products sold by LimX Dynamics Technology Co.,Ltd., covering returns, exchanges, warranty exclusions and a limit on liability; its other tabs (a disclaimer, privacy policy and terms of service) do not load as page text and were not read, so no sale terms beyond the after-sales policy are recorded. The tron1-rl-deploy-ros repository is released under the Apache License 2.0 and carries the full licence text; the limxsdk-lowlevel library the deployment repositories install ships as binary wheels, and no separate licence for it was read.

terms_evidence.scope: After-sales service policy on the Terms & Policies page

not_verified: The documented policy interfaces are LimX's own claims; the Atlas has not verified them. Every source is a LimX web page or a file in a repository LimX can change at any time.
